# Nabbit

> A small island at the top of Windows for videos, file tools and notes in your own Tack. Nabbit v2 is open source, in development and building in public.

Website: https://tanzir71.github.io/nabbit/
Build progress and milestone screenshots: https://tanzir71.github.io/nabbit/#progress
Repository: https://github.com/tanzir71/nabbit

V2 specification and task status: https://github.com/tanzir71/nabbit/blob/main/NABBIT_V2_HANDOFF.md
Implementation log and measured limitations: https://github.com/tanzir71/nabbit/blob/main/PROGRESS.md

## Release state and previews

There is no v2 release yet. The first v2 release follows milestone M12. Use the landing's Follow the build links rather than promising an installer or linking to a nonexistent latest release. The milestone list is the current source for completed work; the v2 handoff distinguishes completed tasks from planned features.

The landing hero shows the current compiled island shell, captured automatically with fixture data and published as an exact lossless image. Its caption and assets/island-hero.json record that scope and provenance. The other activity, download, note and file visuals remain Figma design previews, not screenshots proving those services are implemented. The browser demo simulates the accepted v0.1 tray app. It does not read the clipboard, contact YouTube, launch sidecars or write files.

## V2 product scope

- Windows 10 1809+ and Windows 11, x64 and ARM64 are target platforms; this does not claim every platform has been verified.
- A glanceable island, a tray interface and sticky-note windows, with shared tools and configurable modes.
- Explicit-click video downloads: copied links, top-edge drops, a browser bookmarklet and a hotkey stage a review before a download starts.
- Local file tools and pins: convert or shrink dropped files, move them to a pinned folder, and invoke Send to Nabbit from Explorer. Outputs never overwrite inputs.
- Notes sync with the Tack server the user hosts; local-only notes work without a Tack account. There is no Nabbit cloud or new account.
- Clipboard history, now playing, a focus timer and microphone/camera indicators. Later milestones implement and verify the v2 surfaces and integrations.

## Existing v0.1 foundation

The accepted app is Tauri v2 with a Rust core, React/TypeScript frontend, local SQLite, an event-driven Windows clipboard watcher and yt-dlp/ffmpeg sidecars. It already supplies searchable clipboard history and explicit-click downloads. V2 extends that code rather than replacing it.

## Build and automated checks

npm ci
npm run verify
npm run verify:site
cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --check
cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --test-threads=1

The README documents sidecar setup. Run npm run tauri:dev for the existing tray app; its current shortcut is Ctrl+Shift+V. The v2 handoff documents the planned shortcut changes. The static docs/ website needs no production build, backend, analytics or third-party resource requests.

## Privacy and behavior

- Clipboard history stays in local SQLite under OS app data; no cloud clipboard sync or telemetry.
- Observed links are staged only. Downloads require an explicit click or user hotkey confirmation.
- Retention options are 30, 60 or 90 days; pinned entries survive cleanup.
- Password-manager exclusions, OS concealed-content flags and optional sensitive-text heuristics reduce accidental storage.
- Tack sync goes only to the user's configured server. No hosted Tack credentials or account are needed for local-only use.

Nabbit is a working codename. Download only content you own or have permission to save. DRM-protected media is unsupported; Nabbit is not affiliated with YouTube.
